Definition: a load; by implication, a stroke (others dignity)
BiblicalUsage: This word is a load or a stroke, a weight laid on a person, and it occurs once, when Elihu speaks to Job. My terror shall not make thee afraid, he says, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee, and the word is the heaviness he promises not to lay on his friend. One verse holds a whole promise of gentleness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God does not lay His hand heavily on the suffering, because Elihu's promise is His character: He corrects without crushing.
